The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a local archive (`share.tar.xz`), a direct HTTPS download from the official calibre website (`calibre-${pkgver}-x86_64.txz`), and a GitHub release tarball using the canonical tag URL. All sources are from expected, trustworthy upstream locations. The `sha256sums` are present and non-SKIP, indicating verified downloads.

The top-level scope of the PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments. There is no command substitution, code execution, or network activity triggered during sourcing. The `pkgver()` function is not defined, so no dynamic version calculation occurs. The `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions are present but will not be executed due to the `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` flags. Therefore, no potentially dangerous operations (such as executing `calibre-debug` or building man pages) are triggered during this phase.

The `_build_man.py` script is defined inside a function and written only when `_build_man_pages` is called, which happens during `build()`. It is not evaluated during sourcing or source extraction. No data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unexpected network access occurs during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` commands.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No unsafe operations during source fetch</summary>
</security_assessment>

There is no obfuscated code, no inline network requests outside of the declared sources, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or execute payloads during the sourcing phase. Running these two commands is safe.
</details>
